target.title: Counting attainable ideal sizes
target.label: thm:attainable-count
target.body:
\label{thm:attainable-count}
There exists an absolute integer $B_{\mathrm{cnt}}$ such that, for all integers
$B\ge B_{\mathrm{cnt}}$ and $K$ satisfying
\[
  1\le K\le\frac{(\log B)^2}{100\log\log B},
\]
one has
\[
  |\V(B,K)|\le2^{B-\sqrt B}.
\]
sectionPath: The lower bound as a counting problem

bundle.leadIn: Theorem~\ref{thm:universal-upper} proves the universal upper bound in Theorem~\ref{thm:main}. To obtain a matching lower bound for almost all integers, we count the ideal sizes that can be generated by a small family. For integers $B,K\ge1$, let \[ \V(B,K):=\{\Phi(\mathcal A): \mathcal A=(A_1,\ldots,A_s),\quad 1\le s\le K,\quad |A_i|\le B\text{ for all }i\}. \]

restatement.informalStatement: All logarithms in this statement are to base 2. For positive integers B and K, let V(B,K) be the set of distinct integers n for which there exist a positive integer s with 1 ≤ s ≤ K and finite sets A_1,...,A_s on an arbitrary common ground set such that |A_i| ≤ B for every i and n = |⋃_{i=1}^s P(A_i)|. The sets A_i may be empty, equal, or contain one another; the ambient ground set has no prescribed size bound. There exists an absolute integer B_cnt, independent of K and of all generating families, such that for every integer B ≥ B_cnt and every integer K satisfying 1 ≤ K ≤ (log₂ B)^2 / (100 log₂(log₂ B)), the finite set V(B,K) satisfies |V(B,K)| ≤ 2^(B − √B). The existential threshold may be chosen sufficiently large and positive so that both logarithms and the positive denominator have their ordinary real meanings. Cardinality is coerced to the reals in this inequality; √B is the nonnegative real square root and the right-hand side is real exponentiation with real subtraction. The counted sizes need not lie below 2^B, and each attainable size is counted once regardless of how many families realize it.

vocabulary.name: Finite generating family A = (A_1,...,A_s)
vocabulary.description: A nonempty indexed tuple of finite sets on an arbitrary ground set, with 1 ≤ s ≤ K and each generator of cardinality at most B. Neither generators nor their intersections must be nonempty; repeated and redundant generators are allowed. A finite family of finite sets has finite active union, even if its original ambient type is infinite. Paper: lines 119–124, 197–208, 221–224, 981–985.
vocabulary.leanSketch: A : Fin s → Finset (Fin N), with 1 ≤ s, s ≤ K, and ∀ i, (A i).card ≤ B; N : ℕ is existentially quantified without a cap. Reuse the existing finite-family predicate rather than introducing a new representation.

vocabulary.name: Generated ideal ID and value Φ
vocabulary.description: ID(A) is the union of all powersets P(A_i); Φ(A) is its cardinality. It includes the empty subset whenever the tuple is nonempty, including when every generator is empty. It is not the union of the generators themselves. Paper: lines 197–200 and 221–234.
vocabulary.leanSketch: Reuse AntichainOfGivenSize.generatedIdeal (MainStatement.lean:28–30). For indexed A, Φ is (generatedIdeal (Finset.univ.image A)).card; the existing Section6.generatedIdealIdx representation is bridged to this finite image. Preserve generatedIdeal and alpha unchanged.

vocabulary.name: HasBoundedGeneratingFamily B K n
vocabulary.description: Existing direct audit predicate for membership in the paper's attainable-size set: some nonempty family of at most K finite generators, each of size at most B, generates exactly n subsets. Arbitrary finite ambient size is quantified, not bounded. Removing duplicate entries from the paper's tuple preserves its ideal and leaves at most K distinct generators. Source: Paper/Representation.lean:24–27.
vocabulary.leanSketch: AntichainOfGivenSize.Paper.HasBoundedGeneratingFamily B K n := ∃ m : ℕ, ∃ G : Finset (Finset (Fin m)), G.Nonempty ∧ G.card ≤ K ∧ (∀ A ∈ G, A.card ≤ B) ∧ (generatedIdeal G).card = n

vocabulary.name: Attainable-size set V(B,K)
vocabulary.description: The set of distinct exact natural numbers Φ(A) from all eligible nonempty families. The existing finite implementation is Paper.attainableValues B K; for K > 0, Paper.mem_attainableValues_iff proves exact agreement with HasBoundedGeneratingFamily. It is not a set of residues, a count of families, or a count of isomorphism classes. Paper: lines 981–986; implementation: Paper/Statements.lean:18–23 and Paper/Representation.lean:87–92.
vocabulary.leanSketch: AntichainOfGivenSize.Paper.attainableValues (B K : ℕ) : Finset ℕ := AntichainOfGivenSize.ClusterLowerBound.boundedValues K B; use mem_attainableValues_iff with 0 < K.

vocabulary.name: BoundedProfile and boundedValues (existing implementation vocabulary)
vocabulary.description: A finite Venn multiplicity representation of an exact-K indexed family: each incidence-pattern multiplicity lies in {0,...,B}, the empty-pattern multiplicity is zero, and each generator's load is at most B. Its value is an actual generated ideal cardinality. boundedValues is the image of all such profiles under value. This is already connected to arbitrary finite families and is not an extra paper hypothesis. Sources: LowerBound/BoundedProfiles.lean:17–46,99–102; LowerBound/ClusterImageBound.lean:13–14.
vocabulary.leanSketch: Reuse ClusterLowerBound.BoundedProfile K B and ClusterLowerBound.BoundedProfile.value; boundedValues K B = (Finset.univ : Finset (BoundedProfile K B)).image BoundedProfile.value.

vocabulary.name: Parameter block B, K, B_cnt and AdmissibleBudget
vocabulary.description: B and K are positive integers; B bounds each individual generator and K bounds the number of generators. B_cnt is one absolute existential integer threshold, chosen before universally quantifying B and K. Admissibility means exactly 1 ≤ K and K ≤ (log₂ B)^2/(100 log₂(log₂ B)); the upper bound is a real number, with no change of the constant 100. Paper: lines 981–995.
vocabulary.leanSketch: Reuse Paper.AdmissibleBudget (B K : ℕ) := 1 ≤ K ∧ (K : ℝ) ≤ (Real.logb 2 (B : ℝ)) ^ 2 / (100 * Real.logb 2 (Real.logb 2 (B : ℝ))). Paper.CountingBoundStatement has ∃ B₀ : ℕ, ∀ B K : ℕ, B₀ ≤ B → AdmissibleBudget B K → ...

vocabulary.name: Base-two logarithm and square-root saving
vocabulary.description: The paper explicitly declares all logarithms base 2 at line 215. B − √B is a real exponent, not a truncated natural difference or an integer-rounded square-root saving. These are library operations, listed here to fix the audit convention rather than introduce new definitions.
vocabulary.leanSketch: Real.logb 2 (B : ℝ); Real.logb 2 (Real.logb 2 (B : ℝ)); Real.sqrt (B : ℝ); (2 : ℝ) ^ ((B : ℝ) - Real.sqrt (B : ℝ)).

vocabulary.name: Active ground set and exact-K padding (proof-only)
vocabulary.description: Repeat the final generator to obtain K entries, remove elements lying in no generator, and relabel the union as [N], where 0 ≤ N ≤ KB. [0] is interpreted as empty. These reductions preserve Φ and are not restrictions in the statement. Paper: lines 1011–1017. Existing padding and representation theorems already support them.
vocabulary.leanSketch: Reuse BoundedProfile.pad, BoundedProfile.value_pad, Paper.boundedValues_subset_of_le, and Paper.mem_attainableValues_iff. A finite active universe is represented by Fin N, including Fin 0.

vocabulary.name: Inclusion–exclusion queries I and exponents e_I (proof-only)
vocabulary.description: I is a nonempty subset of the generator index set; e_I = |⋂_{i∈I} A_i| is an integer from 0 through B. Φ = Σ_{I≠∅} (−1)^(|I|+1) 2^e_I is an exact integer identity. Empty queries must not be included. Paper: lines 225–235 and 1019–1025.
vocabulary.leanSketch: I : Finset (Fin K), I.Nonempty; e_I : ℕ. Signed inclusion–exclusion sums have type ℤ. Reuse existing indexed ideal/profile inclusion–exclusion interfaces if needed.

vocabulary.name: λ, h, J, Γ and the scales ρ_j (manuscript proof-only)
vocabulary.description: For B ≥ 2^20, λ = log₂ B, h = floor(λ/4), J = floor(K/h), Γ = B/λ^(6J), and ρ_j = B/λ^(6j) for 0 ≤ j ≤ J+1. λ, Γ and ρ_j are real; h,J are nonnegative integers and h is positive in this range. The selected j lies in {0,...,J}; ρ = ρ_j and ρ′ = ρ_(j+1) = ρ/λ^6, so Γ ≤ ρ ≤ B. These parameters are not part of the theorem's hypotheses. Paper: lines 999–1009 and 1092–1109.
vocabulary.leanSketch: If reproducing this proof, use λ : ℝ, h := ⌊λ / 4⌋₊, J := K / h, Γ := (B : ℝ) / λ ^ (6 * J). The existing endpoint uses different documented integral auxiliary parameters; do not conflate them with these manuscript parameters.

vocabulary.name: Proximity graphs G_θ and packing numbers ν_j (manuscript proof-only)
vocabulary.description: G_θ is the undirected simple graph on [K] whose distinct vertices i,j are adjacent when |A_i ∩ A_j| > B−θ. ν_j is the maximum number of pairwise disjoint connected h-vertex subsets at scale ρ_j. A repeated adjacent packing number yields fine-connected clusters that are also a maximum coarse packing. Connectivity refers to the subgraph on the selected vertices. Paper: lines 1085–1122.
vocabulary.leanSketch: A SimpleGraph (Fin K) with adjacency i ≠ j ∧ (|A_i ∩ A_j| : ℝ) > (B : ℝ) - θ; maximum packings are finite existential witnesses. No new graph implementation is required for reuse of countingBound.

vocabulary.name: Structural header, clusters C_a, residual R, components H_b, roots d_a (manuscript proof-only)
vocabulary.description: A header is j plus a set partition of [K]. Its h-element blocks are the r clusters C_a; smaller blocks H_b are the connected components remaining in the coarse graph after deleting the clusters. R is that residual index set, r ≤ J, |H_b| < h. Blocks are ordered by their least indices and d_a = min C_a. A family is consistent when such a header can arise from the construction. At most (J+1)K^K headers exist; headers need not be unique. Paper: lines 1111–1122 and 1151–1171.

vocabulary.name: Exceptional set U, complement W, incidence words σ and u_I (manuscript proof-only)
vocabulary.description: U consists of active ground elements with nonconstant membership on at least one cluster; equivalently U = ⋃_a ⋃_{i∈C_a}(A_i △ A_(d_a)). Set u=|U| and W=[N]\U. Then u ≤ 2Kρ/λ^6 and generators in a cluster agree on W. Record u and the K-bit incidence words σ(x), x∈U, sorted lexicographically with repetitions. This determines u_I=|U∩⋂_{i∈I}A_i|. Multiplicities must not be discarded. Paper: lines 1175–1199 and 1235–1265.

vocabulary.name: Central queries, S(I), Q(I), w_(S,Q), M_cen and Z (manuscript proof-only)
vocabulary.description: S(I) is the set of clusters met by I; Q(I)=I∩R. A nonempty I is central if Q(I) is empty or contained in one residual component. Record w_(S,Q)=|W∩⋂_{a∈S}A_(d_a)∩⋂_{i∈Q}A_i| for each central pair (S,Q)≠(∅,∅), using [N] for an intersection over an empty index set. Each exponent is at most B; M_cen ≤ 2^J(1+K2^h). For central I, e_I=u_I+w_(S(I),Q(I)). Z is the signed integer inclusion–exclusion sum over central I, determined exactly by the records. Paper: lines 1204–1257.
vocabulary.leanSketch: Use finite index sets and ℕ-valued exponents, but Z : ℤ and the residual Φ−Z : ℤ. Empty intersections use the ambient universe; the pair with both index sets empty is excluded. These are proof descriptions, not proposed new declarations.

vocabulary.name: Tail interval and record-cost parameters d, L_rec (manuscript proof-only)
vocabulary.description: Noncentral exponents are at most B−ρ, giving |Φ−Z| ≤ 2^(B−ρ+K), an interval containing at most 2^(B−ρ+K+2) integers. Set d=2K²/λ⁶ and L_rec=log₂(J+1)+K log₂ K+log₂(KB+1)+2^J(1+K2^h)log₂(B+1)+K+2. Uniformly for admissible K, eventually d≤1/4, L_rec≤Γ/2, and Γ/4≥√B. These are combinatorial counting estimates, not computational resource costs. Paper: lines 1270–1361.

quantity.name: |V(B,K)|
quantity.description: The finite number of distinct exact ideal cardinalities achievable using between 1 and K finite generating sets, each of cardinality at most B, over arbitrary ground sets. The theorem supplies the real upper bound 2^(B−√B) for this count; it does not count generators, profiles, ideals, residues, or algorithm executions.
quantity.crossCheck: Reuse Paper.attainableValues and Finset.card, and cross-check its membership against Paper.mem_attainableValues_iff (Paper/Representation.lean:89–92) and the independently expanded contract in scripts/CheckPaperStatements.lean:57–70. The finite implementation is the image of BoundedProfile.value, an actual generated ideal cardinality. MainStatement.lean:28–30 agrees with Mathlib Finset.powerset (membership means subset) and finite union. Mathlib Data/Finset/Powerset.lean and Data/Finset/Card.lean provide powersets and cardinality; no library-level notion of this specialized attainable-value set needs to be reinvented. Do not substitute boundedResidues.

algorithm.name: None: deterministic counting theorem

canonicalTarget.statement: Exactly Theorem 7.1 (thm:attainable-count): there exists one absolute integer threshold B_cnt such that for every integer B ≥ B_cnt and every integer K with 1 ≤ K ≤ (log₂ B)^2/(100 log₂(log₂ B)), the number of all distinct attainable ideal sizes from nonempty families of at most K finite sets, each of size at most B, is at most 2^(B−√B). Reuse AntichainOfGivenSize.Paper.countingBound : CountingBoundStatement with the proved representation equivalence; this is an interface to an existing proof, not a newly derived counting theorem.
nonGoals: No proof or restatement of universal upper bounds, the bit/block matching constructions, the main theorem, density-one statements, extremal order, or the subsequent dyadic probability corollary.
No algorithm, sampler, probability monad, operational semantics, runtime, space bound, or enumeration procedure.
No requirement to reproduce every intermediate manuscript equation or the streamlined header product when reusing the already proved endpoint.
No optimization or requirement to expose a least threshold; the existing proof's witness 2^(2^20) is sufficient but is not prescribed by the manuscript.
No restriction of B to powers of two or a sparse sequence; no replacement by an infinitely-often lower bound, asymptotic-O estimate, residue count, or weaker budget constant.
No changes to generatedIdeal, alpha, completed library files, manuscript, checksum, dependency pins, audit registry, or independently expanded contracts in this pass.

claimLedger.claim: One absolute threshold works for every B above it and every K in the exact stated real-log budget, and |V(B,K)| ≤ 2^(B−√B).
V(B,K) consists exactly of numerical ideal sizes from nonempty families of at most K generators of individual size at most B, with no ambient cap.
Repeating a final generator and relabelling the active ground set preserve the ideal size and give N ≤ KB.
Φ equals the complete signed inclusion–exclusion sum over nonempty queries.
Each eligible family admits a structural header; there are at most (J+1)K^K possible headers.
The exceptional set has size at most 2Kρ/λ^6 and cluster members agree off it.
The incidence record and central exponent transcript determine the exact signed central sum Z.
There are at most (KB+1)2^(2K²ρ/λ⁶) incidence records and (B+1)^(2^J(1+K2^h)) central transcripts.
Every noncentral exponent is at most B−ρ; the signed tail lies in an interval with at most 2^(B−ρ+K+2) integer values.
For each header the attainable-value count is bounded by the product of the incidence, transcript and tail-interval counts.
Uniformly in admissible K, Γ≥2^(7λ/10), eventually d≤1/4 and L_rec≤Γ/2, and eventually Γ/4≥√B; summing over headers yields the stronger intermediate bound 2^(B−Γ/4).
The existing endpoint proves the exact target with a different, larger clustered record encoding; identify reuse honestly and preserve the correspondence note.
This target asserts no probabilistic or computational resource result; the following uniformly sampled dyadic corollary is separate.

hypothesisLedger.hypothesis: B and K are integers, with B ≥ one absolute sufficiently large threshold and K ≥ 1.
hypothesisLedger.why: Preserve the integer input domain and uniform existential threshold. Natural parameters are equivalent on this positive range.
The precise real bound and constant 100 are part of the result, not adjustable proof parameters.

hypothesisLedger.hypothesis: A witnessing tuple has 1 ≤ s ≤ K and |A_i| ≤ B for all i.
hypothesisLedger.why: These define V(B,K). They are not additional universal family arguments or assumptions external to attainable-value membership.

hypothesisLedger.hypothesis: Each generator is a finite set.
hypothesisLedger.why: Powerset and union cardinalities must be finite; the paper's finite-set setting is preserved by Finset.

hypothesisLedger.hypothesis: B > 2, log₂ B > 1, and log₂(log₂ B) > 0.
hypothesisLedger.why: Choose or enlarge the single existential threshold; do not require separate logarithm-positivity inputs or use totalized logs at small B.

hypothesisLedger.hypothesis: B ≥ 2^20 and h=floor(log₂ B/4) > 0 in the manuscript proof.
hypothesisLedger.why: This is a preliminary range for auxiliary estimates, not the final threshold claim.

hypothesisLedger.hypothesis: The family has exactly K indexed entries.
hypothesisLedger.why: Pad by repeating the last generator; nonemptiness makes this possible. Existing representation and padding lemmas already do this.

hypothesisLedger.hypothesis: The active ground set is [N] with N ≤ KB.
hypothesisLedger.why: Delete unused elements and relabel the finite union; no ambient-size cap may be added to membership.

hypothesisLedger.hypothesis: The generators are an antichain, minimal, distinct, nonempty sets, or have sizes exactly B.
hypothesisLedger.why: Only the index family is nonempty, and only upper size bounds are assumed. Minimality implies an antichain in the preliminaries but is not required here.

hypothesisLedger.hypothesis: Balancedness or restrictions on intermediate-order intersections.
hypothesisLedger.why: The manuscript expressly disclaims these restrictions.

hypothesisLedger.hypothesis: B is a power of two, K ≥ h, or J ≥ 1.
hypothesisLedger.why: Every sufficiently large integer B and every admissible K are covered, including K<h and J=0.

hypothesisLedger.hypothesis: An attainable n lies below 2^B, in a specified dyadic block, or is a residue modulo 2^B.
hypothesisLedger.why: Those restrictions belong to later applications, not the attainable-value definition or this theorem.

hypothesisLedger.hypothesis: A selected header, maximum packing, and record-size inequalities exist.
hypothesisLedger.why: They are proved within the counting argument; they must never become unproved hypotheses of the public endpoint.

modelingChoices.decision: Reuse the existing ℕ statement with K≥1 and an existential sufficiently large positive B threshold. Explain the equivalence with the paper's integer quantifiers.
modelingChoices.reason: All permitted integers are nonnegative once the threshold is chosen positive; the theorem is not extended to arbitrary real B or K.
modelingChoices.downstreamRisk: Do not silently restrict to a special sequence or let a threshold depend on K.

modelingChoices.item: One-based [s] and [N], including the all-empty family.
modelingChoices.decision: Use Fin s and Fin N as reindexings; allow N=0 and interpret [0] as empty.
modelingChoices.reason: The paper's interval convention does not explicitly define [0], but empty generators are allowed and the active union may be empty.
modelingChoices.downstreamRisk: Adding N≥1 or requiring a nonempty generator would alter membership and could lose the attainable value 1.

modelingChoices.item: Tuples versus Finset families and exact-K profiles.
modelingChoices.decision: Reuse the proved representation equivalence, deduplication of tuples, and padding by repetition.
modelingChoices.reason: Order and repeated generators do not change a union of powersets; shorter nonempty tuples can be padded without changing their value.
modelingChoices.downstreamRisk: Do not count tuple lengths or multiplicities as ideal sizes; do not apply the equivalence at K=0.

modelingChoices.decision: Quantify an arbitrary finite ambient size in the direct predicate; treat finite active support and relabelling as justified reductions.
modelingChoices.reason: Finite many finite generators have finite union, and unused ambient points affect no subset in the generated ideal.
modelingChoices.downstreamRisk: Do not replace the individual bound B by a fixed universe Fin B or an independent input cap.

modelingChoices.decision: Reuse the finite image attainableValues and its membership equivalence, preserving exact natural values before taking Finset.card.
modelingChoices.reason: This avoids any hidden infinite-set cardinality convention and counts each attained number once.
modelingChoices.downstreamRisk: Residue images may collapse distinct values; Set.ncard without finiteness or a family count would not be an adequate semantic substitute.

modelingChoices.item: Real logs, real square root, real subtraction and real power.
modelingChoices.decision: Keep Real.logb 2, Real.sqrt, and real exponentiation in the expanded theorem. Auxiliary integral bounds are confined to the existing proof.
modelingChoices.reason: Rounding or changing the log base changes the exact budget or saving; natural subtraction truncates.
modelingChoices.downstreamRisk: Compare the expanded statement against scripts/CheckPaperStatements.lean:65–70, not merely an alias with a matching name.

modelingChoices.item: Threshold and the preliminary B ≥ 2^20 range.
modelingChoices.decision: State only existence of a sufficiently large absolute integer threshold. Record that the existing certificate uses 2^(2^20); do not attribute that specific witness to the manuscript.
modelingChoices.reason: The paper's final λ₀ is chosen after several uniform eventual estimates.
modelingChoices.downstreamRisk: Claiming B_cnt=2^20 from the opening proof paragraph would overstate the manuscript.

modelingChoices.item: Reuse rather than rederive the counting proof.
modelingChoices.decision: Use Paper.countingBound and Paper.mem_attainableValues_iff as the endpoint and its semantic interface.
modelingChoices.reason: Both already exist with the exact required constants, quantifiers and conclusion; no missing counting proof obligation was found for this target.
modelingChoices.downstreamRisk: Do not overwrite completed files, invent replacement lemma names, or call a wrapper a new proof of the counting theorem.

modelingChoices.item: Different proof representation in existing Lean.
modelingChoices.decision: Preserve the documented fact that the checked proof uses a larger clustered encoding and different auxiliary integral parameters, rather than the manuscript's exact fixed-header product.
modelingChoices.reason: docs/current-paper.md:166–175 explicitly records this difference while preserving the endpoint.
modelingChoices.downstreamRisk: An interface reusing the endpoint must not claim that every displayed intermediate manuscript estimate was newly formalized.

modelingChoices.decision: No Program or Pseudocode algorithm contract is needed. Graphs, packings, records and transcripts are proof-only vocabulary.
modelingChoices.reason: The statement bounds a mathematical set cardinality and specifies no run or output procedure.
modelingChoices.downstreamRisk: Do not add probability-one claims or resource annotations to deterministic cardinality inequalities.

modelingChoices.item: J=0, no clusters, and empty central index choices.
modelingChoices.decision: Retain K<h and J=0. Allow an empty cluster collection and empty U; exclude only the pair (S,Q)=(∅,∅) from recorded central queries.
modelingChoices.reason: These cases are permitted by the definitions and fit the proof; at least one selected generator keeps each recorded exponent ≤B.
modelingChoices.downstreamRisk: Extra positivity on J or including the empty query would change the proof and possibly its exponent bounds.

modelingChoices.decision: Report only source inspection in this reader pass. Let later Tex2Lean passes generate their own plans, status and handoff evidence.
modelingChoices.reason: Reading an existing proof and historical checks is not a fresh build or integration check.
modelingChoices.downstreamRisk: Do not fabricate workflow output, mark newly generated targets proved by hand, or claim current successful integration.

program: No algorithm is present. Do not implement a sampler, maximum-packing search, enumeration program, cost semantics, or probability monad for this target.
If a scaffold requires Model/Program.lean, keep it limited to references to the mathematical model; do not invent an operational contract.
Reuse existing generatedIdeal, HasBoundedGeneratingFamily, attainableValues and AdmissibleBudget definitions and their proved links; preserve alpha unchanged.
pseudocode: No algorithm listing is available or required. The paper's record/transcript construction is an explanatory proof encoding, not a mandated executable program.

import AntichainOfGivenSize.Analysis.AttainableValuesMembershipProof

/-!
# The attainable-size counting surface

This surface reuses the existing definitions without introducing a second
representation. Their defining vocabulary is in `Model/CountingVocabulary.lean`;
the original proof modules import those same declarations. Its sole cross-check spells out the semantics of the counted
values; the later proof pass can reuse `Paper.mem_attainableValues_iff`.
-/

namespace AntichainOfGivenSize.Model

/-! ## Vocabulary

`AntichainOfGivenSize.generatedIdeal G` is the finite union of the powersets
of the generators in `G`, implemented by `Finset.biUnion` and `Finset.powerset`.
Its `Finset.card` counts subsets, not elements in the union of the generators.

`Paper.HasBoundedGeneratingFamily B K n` quantifies an arbitrary natural
ambient size `N` and a family `G : Finset (Finset (Fin N))`. It requires
`G.Nonempty`, `G.card ≤ K`, every generator's cardinality at most `B`, and
`(generatedIdeal G).card = n`. There is no upper bound on `N`. In particular,
`Fin 0` is allowed. The family, rather than each generator, must be nonempty:
a nonempty family of empty generators has generated-ideal cardinality `1`.
Tuple order and repeated generators do not change this union of powersets;
the existing membership bridge accounts for deduplication and padding.
Redundant generators are permitted.

`Paper.AdmissibleBudget B K` is exactly `1 ≤ K` together with the real bound
`(K : ℝ) ≤ (Real.logb 2 (B : ℝ)) ^ 2 /
  (100 * Real.logb 2 (Real.logb 2 (B : ℝ)))`.
The headline expands this budget. All logarithms are base two; `Real.sqrt`
and real exponentiation retain the paper's unrounded square-root saving.
-/

/-! ## The quantity

The quantity bounded by the headline is
`((Paper.attainableValues B K).card : ℝ)`. The existing finite set
`Paper.attainableValues` is the image of the bounded profiles under their
exact generated-ideal cardinalities. Each natural value is counted once,
with no residue reduction or restriction to values below `2 ^ B`.

The cross-check below exposes the family semantics of this implementation.
It is deliberately guarded by `0 < K`; in the headline's range this follows
from the first conjunct of the budget, rather than a separate assumption.
-/

/-- Cross-check `Paper.attainableValues` against the expanded definition of
`Paper.HasBoundedGeneratingFamily`, using the existing result
`Paper.mem_attainableValues_iff`. This also matches the independent membership
contract in `scripts/CheckPaperStatements.lean`. -/
theorem attainableValues_membership {B K n : ℕ} (hK : 0 < K) :
    n ∈ Paper.attainableValues B K ↔
      ∃ N : ℕ, ∃ G : Finset (Finset (Fin N)),
        G.Nonempty ∧ G.card ≤ K ∧
          (∀ A ∈ G, A.card ≤ B) ∧ (generatedIdeal G).card = n := by
    exact AntichainOfGivenSize.Analysis.AttainableCountProof.attainableValuesMembership (B := B) (K := K) (n := n) hK

end AntichainOfGivenSize.Model

files.contents:
import AntichainOfGivenSize.Model.Prelude
import AntichainOfGivenSize.Model.Prior
import AntichainOfGivenSize.Meta.ModelClosure
import AntichainOfGivenSize.Analysis.AttainableCountProof

/-!
# Counting attainable ideal sizes

Theorem 7.1 (`thm:attainable-count`) has one deterministic cardinality claim.
Its intended proof interface reuses `AntichainOfGivenSize.Paper.countingBound`;
it does not rederive the counting argument. The existing proof uses the larger
clustered encoding documented in `docs/current-paper.md`, rather than a
line-by-line transcription of the manuscript's fixed-header product.

Natural parameters represent the paper's integers on the positive range:
the absolute existential threshold may be enlarged to make `B` positive,
and the budget requires `1 ≤ K`. That threshold is independent of `K` and
is not identified with the proof's preliminary bound `2 ^ 20`.
The budget also supplies `0 < K` for the membership cross-check in Prelude.

The defining vocabulary of `Paper.attainableValues` is in
`Model/CountingVocabulary.lean`, retaining the existing names and definitions.
The statement's complete quantity dependency chain therefore lies within the
audit surface, while the counting and representation proofs stay outside it.
-/

namespace AntichainOfGivenSize

/-- Theorem 7.1: one absolute threshold gives the stated bound on the number
of distinct attainable ideal sizes for every admissible pair `B, K`.
The real arithmetic and the constant `100` are expanded for comparison with
the manuscript and `scripts/CheckPaperStatements.lean`. -/
theorem attainable_count (hprior : Prior) :
    ∃ B₀ : ℕ, ∀ B K : ℕ, B₀ ≤ B →
      (1 ≤ K ∧ (K : ℝ) ≤ (Real.logb 2 (B : ℝ)) ^ 2 /
        (100 * Real.logb 2 (Real.logb 2 (B : ℝ)))) →
      ((Paper.attainableValues B K).card : ℝ) ≤
        (2 : ℝ) ^ ((B : ℝ) - Real.sqrt (B : ℝ)) := by
    exact AntichainOfGivenSize.Analysis.AttainableCountProof.attainableCount hprior

end AntichainOfGivenSize

interfacePlan.skipped: the paper states no algorithm, so there is no `Model/Program.lean` and nothing for `Interface/` to translate

definitionOfDone: The mechanical checks pass. They are run by the extension over the whole project between rounds — the build, the `sorry` warnings, the axiom profile of every headline, a sweep for escape hatches, the closure checks, and the two layout rules — and what they find comes back to you as the next round's brief. Build the modules you created and read their errors; do not try to run the gate.
`#print axioms` on the capstone reports exactly the three ambient axioms — propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound — and nothing else.
No `declaration uses sorry` warning anywhere in the build output.
A grep sweep for `sorry`, `admit`, `native_decide` and `axiom` over the project comes back clean, and agrees with the other two checks.
The closure checks have been observed to *fail* on a deliberately broken control, so that their passing means something.

The audit surface still states the paper's theorem: every claim the paper makes is in it, and nothing was weakened to make a proof go through. No script decides this one — the extension's handoff check reads the paper and the surface side by side, and it runs as the last step of a run.

risks.risk: A round closes the capstone by leaning on lemmas that are themselves still `sorry`, which looks like progress and is not.
risks.mitigation: The open-goal list is read out of the Lean sources every round, so a lemma left `sorry` stays on it however the declaration above it was closed.

risks.risk: An agent weakens an intermediate lemma until it is provable but useless.
risks.mitigation: Whatever depends on it stops building, and the next round re-reads the sources rather than the plan.
